# todo-app

A full-stack To Do list for an engineering challenge. A user signs in and manages only their own tasks: create, read, update, delete, reorder and search, with a detail screen per task and a responsive UI. `backend/` is a REST API in Python (FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy, alembic, Postgres). `frontend/` is a React SPA in TypeScript (Vite, TanStack Query, Zod, Tailwind). The app is built to run as more than one backend replica: containers first, then a local k3d cluster, then AKS.

## Read first
- `docs/kickoff.md`: the requirements, the human's feedback and the locked decisions. It is the spec; plans in `docs/plans/` build on it.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: branches and deploy stages (§1), branch names and PR labels (§2), test gates (§5), the kind-stop protocol (§8), human-runs-it for ops and deploys (§11), secrets (§12).
- `.claude/rules/`: working agreement, coding standards, testing and git rules load every session. Python, database, API contract, TypeScript, React and deployment rules load when you touch matching files.
- `backend/CLAUDE.md` and `frontend/CLAUDE.md`: each app's commands, config and layout.
- Skills: `/repo-sync` at the start of a session, `/verify` before saying done or committing, `/claude-docs-check` then `/raise-pr` to open a PR.

## Hard requirements that shape every change
- Test-driven: red, green, refactor, and every commit is green. Each test layer owns different failures; no test repeats another layer's job (`testing.md`).
- Functional and declarative: a pure core with an I/O shell, no mutated inputs, composition and higher-order functions, `map`/`filter`/`reduce` and comprehensions, the right data structure (`coding-standards.md`).
- Async through high-level abstractions: async FastAPI and SQLAlchemy with `TaskGroup` on the backend, TanStack Query on the frontend.
- Logs that help monitoring stay (startup, ready, caught errors with context); logs added only to debug go before the commit. No `TODO` or `FIXME` in code.
- HTTP semantics as in `api-contract.md`, including 400 (not FastAPI's default 422) for validation errors and 404 for another user's task.

## Commands
```bash
python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py      # task markers, debuggers, focused tests, debug-only logs; CI runs it
GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) docker compose up --build --wait   # the stack, on http://localhost:8080
docker compose down                   # stop it; `down -v` also deletes the database
```
Each app's own commands are in its `CLAUDE.md`; `CONTRIBUTING.md` § 5 lists every gate.

The stack is Postgres, a one-shot `migrate` service, two API replicas and nginx. It needs a `.env` in the repo root, which the human creates once with `cp .env.example .env`. Three suites run against it:
- Live-server e2e, `tests/e2e/live/` (pytest, Python 3.14.8): `cd tests/e2e/live && uv run pytest`. CI also runs ruff and mypy there.
- Browser journeys, `tests/e2e/browser/` (Playwright, Chromium): from that folder, `npm ci && npx playwright install chromium` once, then `npm run check && npm test`. The HTML report goes to `playwright-report/`.
- Load, `tests/load/` (k6 in a compose container): `GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) docker compose --profile load run --rm k6 run /scripts/journey.js`. `VUS` and `HOLD` set the users and the hold time (200 and 3m by default). `python3 tests/load/run_stepped.py` steps up the users to find the capacity. Results go to `tests/load/results/`. Run load tests with the lead present.

## Config and secrets
- `.env.example` is the only env file an agent may read or edit, by that exact name; it holds safe local values and never a real secret. Never read or edit `.env` or any other `.env.*` file, or key material. Hooks and the deny list block them, and a Bash command that only names such a file is blocked too. When a setting is needed, add it to `.env.example` with a safe local value; the human copies it into `.env` and sets real values there.
- `.mcp.json` configures Claude Code's own MCP servers. It is not the app's config.

## Workspace rules
This repo sits inside a larger workspace whose `.claude/rules/` also load. The general rules there apply (PR card, assignee, no auto-reviewers, typed boundaries, failure handling). The product-specific protocols do not: seed compile and migrate, planner templates, ThinkingBlock, user cleanup scripts, turbo logs, and sibling contract repos. There are no sibling repos here.

## Gotchas
- `transcript-backup.py` snapshots the session transcript into `.ai-transcripts/` before and after every compaction and at session end, and blocks a compaction it could not back up. The snapshots are the record of AI use; never delete them.
- macOS ships bash 3.2 and Python 3.9. Repo scripts and hooks are Python standard library and start with `from __future__ import annotations`, so they run on a reviewer's Mac; CI tests them on 3.9 and 3.13. The guard hooks fail closed: a crash denies the call.
- The Bash guards read every word of a command, heredoc bodies included. Text that names an env file or a reader program trips them: write prose with the Write tool, and commit such messages with `git commit -F <file>`.
- The three Bash guards share `.claude/hooks/shell_words.py`. A change there changes all three; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/hooks/tests` under `/usr/bin/python3` as well as 3.13.
- The branch-protection hook blocks every commit on `main`. Branch first.
- FastAPI answers validation errors with 422 unless the app's handler maps them. Keep the handler; the contract says 400.
- Set `GIT_SHA` on every compose command that builds or runs, `docker compose run` included. Images are tagged with it and fall back to `local`; a command under another tag makes compose recreate the running stack.
- `tests/load/run_stepped.py` runs `docker compose down -v` before each step. That deletes the local database and every account in it.
- The k6 image runs as uid 12345 and writes its summaries to `tests/load/results/` through a bind mount. Docker Desktop on a Mac maps that user to yours; on a Linux host the folder must be writable by uid 12345 first.
- The browser journeys fail on any `console.error`, uncaught exception or CSP violation in the page, except a 401 from `/api/` (`tests/e2e/browser/fixtures.ts`). They run on a CPU throttled six times, so a race a fast laptop hides fails here, not only in CI.

## Branches and deploy
- Each round has an integration branch, `round/<n>-<name>`, and one parent PR into `main` that merges only when the round is done and tested. Work on a branch off the round branch and open a child PR into it; the human lead reviews every PR. Child PRs are squash-merged, the parent is rebase-merged (`CONTRIBUTING.md` § 1). Releases are `vX.Y.Z` tags; a tag is never moved.
- CI runs on every PR: hygiene, the backend and frontend gates, and an `e2e` job that builds the stack and runs the live and browser suites against it.
- Deploy stages are in `.claude/rules/deployment.md`. The human reviews every deployment artifact before it is applied, and runs anything against AKS.
- Guards: a hook blocks commits and pushes on `main` and on round branches, force pushes, `--no-verify` and tag moves. `git push`, `gh pr create`, `kubectl apply`/`delete`, `helm` and `az` always ask. PR titles must be Conventional Commits. A PR also needs a docs decision from `/claude-docs-check`.

## Scope
Change only what the task names. Do not fix nearby code or add tests the change does not need. Unrelated problems go in a one-line follow-up note.

# Working agreement

How this team works with Claude Code. Applies to every session in this repo.

- Write in plain English: chat, docs, commit messages, PR text, code comments. Short sentences. If a simpler word carries the same meaning, use it.
- Lead with the answer or the outcome. Supporting detail comes after; leave out steps that do not change what the reader does next. Bullets for parallel items.
- Plan, align, execute. For anything beyond a small change, state the approach in a few lines and get a yes before building. Ask when different readings of the task would lead to different work. Do not ask about routine choices.
- Estimate in agent-pair time, not human-solo time. A well-aligned agent and human pair finishes in roughly a twentieth of the solo-human time. Give estimates as bounded work ("4 file edits, 1 migration, 1 PR" or "within a session"), never as human days. Name external waits (CI, deploys, reviews) separately.
- At the start of a session, run `/repo-sync` before writing code. Never switch or pull a repo that has uncommitted work without saying so.
- Stay in scope. Change only what the task names. Unrelated problems become a one-line follow-up note, not an inline fix.
- When a written plan or spec and the situation disagree, stop and ask. Never deviate silently, even when the deviation looks like an improvement. The spec for this repo is `docs/kickoff.md`, then the plan docs in `docs/plans/`.
- Report outcomes as they are. Failing tests are reported as failing, with output. Skipped steps are named. "Done" means `/verify` passed.

# Git and pull requests

## Branches
- Each round has an integration branch, `round/<n>-<name>`, created from `main` by the human. Work on a branch off the current round branch: `feature/<name>`, `fix/<name>`, `chore/<name>`, `docs/<name>`, `refactor/<name>`, `perf/<name>`, `test/<name>`, `ci/<name>`. Lowercase, hyphens, no personal names.
- Never commit on `main` or a round branch. Never force-push a shared branch. Never `--no-verify`. A hook blocks all three.
- Releases are `vX.Y.Z` tags on `main`. A tag is never moved or deleted; a wrong tag is fixed by cutting the next version. A hook blocks tag moves.

## Commits
- One logical change per commit, and every commit is green (see `testing.md`). Conventional Commits: `type(scope): subject`. Types: feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, perf, test, ci, build, revert, release. Scopes: `api`, `web`, `db`, `auth`, `deploy`, `claude`, `round-<n>` (a parent PR), or none. Subject starts lowercase, no trailing period, imperative mood.
- The body says why, not what.
- Add `Refs: #<issue>` or `Refs: docs/plans/<file>.md` when there is one.

## Pull requests
- Run `/raise-pr`. It shows the card (title, branch, base, assignee, label, summary) and waits for a yes.
- The title follows the commit format. A hook blocks titles that do not.
- Assignee is the human whose git identity is on the commits. No reviewers unless the human names them.
- Label: exactly one, taken from the branch prefix through the table in `CONTRIBUTING.md` § 2. A prefix with no row in that table is a gap; ask before raising.
- Description: what, why, how to test, risks and rollback. Link sources instead of restating them.
- Child PRs target the round branch. One parent PR per round (`round/<n>-<name>` → `main`, label `round`) stays a draft until the round is done and tested; link each child PR from it.
- The human lead reviews every PR. Child PRs are squash-merged (the PR title becomes the commit subject, so it must be Conventional), and the parent PR is rebase-merged into `main`. The human lead has the final call.
- `git push` and `gh pr create` always ask before running. That is intended.

# Testing

Robust testing is a hard requirement, and so is test-driven development. Applies to every change.

## Test first
- Red, green, refactor. Write the test, run it and watch it fail for the expected reason, write the least code that makes it pass, then clean up with the test still green. Run the red step in the session so the transcript shows it.
- Every commit is green. All suites that the change touches pass before `git commit`; a failing test is never committed. A commit holds the test and the code that passes it together.
- New behaviour gets a test in the same commit. A bug fix starts with a test that reproduces the bug.

## Each layer earns its place
Test a behaviour once, at the lowest layer that can catch it. A higher layer covers only what the lower layers cannot see. Before adding a test, name the failure it catches that no existing test catches; if there is none, do not add it.

| Layer | Tool | Owns | Does not re-test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend unit | pytest | pure functions in the core: ordering, search filters, validation, token and password helpers | anything HTTP or SQL |
| Backend integration | pytest, httpx `ASGITransport`, a real database | each endpoint's contract: status codes, response shape, auth, ownership, persistence | the pure rules already unit-tested, beyond one case that proves the wiring |
| Frontend unit and component | Vitest (its API matches Jest's), React Testing Library, MSW at the `fetch` boundary | pure helpers, hooks, and each screen's states: loading, empty, error, success, validation | backend rules |
| Live-server e2e | pytest against the running stack (compose, then k3d) | what only a deployed stack shows: migrations ran, the proxy and cookie path, ingress and routing, a session issued by one replica accepted by another | endpoint contracts |
| Browser e2e | Playwright against the running stack | a few complete user journeys: sign in, create, reorder, search, edit, delete, sign out; and the small-screen layout | screen states and endpoint contracts |
| Load | k6 from its container against the running stack | latency and error budgets at 200 concurrent users, data consistency afterwards, and the round's capacity figure from a stepped run | correctness of single requests |

## Concurrency
- Each race in the spec has an integration test named after it that fires the requests together with `asyncio.TaskGroup` against a real Postgres. Each one must fail when its guard is removed; show that once, in the session.
- A fixture runs the backend suite in asyncio debug mode with a 50 ms slow-callback threshold and fails any test during which the event loop was blocked.
- The race tests and the load tests are run with the lead present: show the scripts and budgets first, then walk through the results.

## Mechanics
- Mock at the boundary (the HTTP client, `fetch`, the clock), never inside the code under test. Nothing in a unit suite opens a socket.
- Tests are independent and order-free. Each builds its own data through factories or fixtures; none relies on another's leftovers.
- Assert on behaviour a user or caller can see: status, body, rendered text and roles. Never on private attributes or CSS class names.
- One reason to fail per test. The name says the behaviour: `test_reorder_rejects_task_owned_by_another_user`, `it("shows the empty state when the user has no tasks")`.
- Coverage is a floor, not a target: CI fails below the threshold set in `pyproject.toml` and `vitest.config.ts`. A line covered by a test that asserts nothing is not covered.
- Report results as they are. "128 passed" means you saw it. Name the suite and the stack it ran against.

# Coding standards

Applies to `backend/` (Python) and `frontend/` (TypeScript). The path-scoped rules add the language detail.

## General
- Minimal code. No speculative abstractions. No options nobody asked for.
- Concise but descriptive. A name says what a thing is or does; a reader should not need the comment to follow the code.
- Prefer editing an existing file to adding one. Delete what is unused. No dead branches.
- Every public function, class, component and type carries a one-line summary in the language's doc format (Google-style docstrings in Python, JSDoc in TypeScript). Sections (`Args:`, `@param`) only when they add something the signature does not say. Other comments are single line and only where the code cannot say it. No comment blocks. No commented-out code.
- Comments are written for someone new to the codebase. A hard-to-follow part gets a single-line comment above it saying concisely what happens there. Never cite the spec, the plan, decision or question ids (`D14`, `Q-4`), review rounds or the history of a choice. Where a library's behaviour is the reason, link that library's docs; where a module has its own page under `docs/`, link that page.
- Every change is verifiable. If you cannot test it, say so before shipping it.
- Match the surrounding code's style, not its gaps.

## Functional and declarative style (a hard requirement)
- Functional core, imperative shell. Domain logic (validation, ordering, search filters, mapping rows to responses) is pure functions with no I/O. Routers, repositories and React components are the thin shell that does I/O and calls the core.
- Never mutate an input. Return a new value. Python: frozen dataclasses, Pydantic models with `frozen=True` where they flow through the core, tuples over lists for fixed data. TypeScript: `const`, `readonly`, spread, `toSorted`/`toSpliced`/`with` over `sort`/`splice`.
- Prefer expressions to statements: `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, comprehensions and generator expressions over loops that append into an accumulator. Use a loop only when it reads more clearly, and never just to mutate an outer variable.
- Compose small functions instead of writing one long one. Higher-order functions where they remove repetition: FastAPI `Depends` factories, decorators, hooks that take a query function, comparator builders. Do not add one for a single caller.
- Pick the data structure for the access pattern: a dict or `Map` for lookup by id, a set for membership, a list or tuple for order. Say why in review when it is not obvious.
- No hidden shared mutable state: no module-level caches that requests write to, no singletons holding request data.

## Async and concurrency (a hard requirement)
- Use the high-level abstraction, never hand-rolled threads or callbacks. Backend: `async def` handlers, the async SQLAlchemy session, `asyncio.TaskGroup` (or `gather`) when independent awaits can run together. Frontend: TanStack Query for all server state (caching, retries, cancellation, optimistic updates with rollback), never `useEffect` plus `fetch`.
- Never block the event loop. CPU-heavy work (password hashing) runs through `asyncio.to_thread` or the library's async API.

## Boundaries and types
- Every value that crosses a boundary (HTTP body, database row, token claims, storage, URL params) is a typed model, validated right after it is read: Pydantic in Python, Zod in TypeScript. Field access happens on the validated value. No `dict[str, Any]`, `any` or `Record<string, unknown>` for a known shape.
- Type hints on every parameter and return value, tests included. TypeScript is `strict`; no `any`, no `as unknown as`, no `@ts-ignore`.

## Logging
- Logs exist to monitor the running app and find bugs. Keep every line that does that: startup and ready, shutdown, a caught exception with its context, a request that failed auth or validation at WARNING, a degraded path taken.
- Remove every line added only to chase a bug during development before the commit. A log line that would not help someone on call is noise.
- Backend: `log = logging.getLogger(__name__)`, never `print`. Frontend: `console.info` for lifecycle, `console.warn` and `console.error` for failures; never `console.log` or `console.debug`. ESLint enforces the frontend list.
- WARNING and ERROR lines say where, why and what happens next, with ids as key=value (`user_id=`, `task_id=`, `request_id=`). Never log secrets, passwords, tokens or full request bodies.

## Hygiene
- No `TODO`, `FIXME`, `XXX` or `HACK` in code. A follow-up goes in the PR description or an issue.
- No `debugger`, `breakpoint()`, `pdb`, or focused tests (`.only`). `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py` checks all of this and runs in CI and in `/verify`.
- Secrets never appear in code, logs, tests, or chat. `.env` files and key material are off limits; a hook enforces this. Anything bundled into the frontend is public.
</system-reminder>

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.
</system-reminder>

The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

+# The API: three pods, one uvicorn process each, one per node. Any pod serves any request.
+apiVersion: apps/v1
+kind: Deployment
+metadata:
+  name: api
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+spec:
+  replicas: 3
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+  strategy:
+    # A new pod is ready before an old one leaves, so three keep serving through a release.
+    rollingUpdate:
+      maxSurge: 1
+      maxUnavailable: 0
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+    spec:
+      automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      # Covers the 20 s preStop sleep, uvicorn's 20 s drain and a margin.
+      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
+      topologySpreadConstraints:
+        - maxSkew: 1
+          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
+          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
+          labelSelector:
+            matchLabels:
+              app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+          # Counts only pods of the same release, so a rolling update can always place its new pod.
+          matchLabelKeys: [pod-template-hash]
+      securityContext:
+        runAsNonRoot: true
+        runAsUser: 10001
+        runAsGroup: 10001
+        seccompProfile:
+          type: RuntimeDefault
+      containers:
+        - name: api
+          image: todo-api
+          ports:
+            - name: http
+              containerPort: 8000
+          envFrom:
+            - configMapRef:
+                name: todo-config
+          env:
+            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: todo-db
+                  key: password
+            # Kubernetes fills in $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) from the variable above.
+            - name: DATABASE_URL
+              value: postgresql+asyncpg://todo:$(POSTGRES_PASSWORD)@db:5432/todo
+            - name: JWT_SECRET
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: todo-api
+                  key: jwt-secret
+          startupProbe:
+            httpGet:
+              path: /livez
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 2
+            failureThreshold: 30
+          livenessProbe:
+            httpGet:
+              path: /livez
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 10
+            failureThreshold: 3
+          readinessProbe:
+            httpGet:
+              path: /readyz
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 5
+            failureThreshold: 2
+          lifecycle:
+            # Kubernetes takes the pod out of the Service at once, but nginx re-reads DNS only every 10 s and
+            # the cluster DNS caches for 5 s. Serving 20 s more covers that, then SIGTERM starts uvicorn's drain.
+            # https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/#hook-handler-implementations
+            preStop:
+              sleep:
+                seconds: 20
+          resources:
+            requests:
+              cpu: 500m
+              memory: 256Mi
+            # One core is the most a single uvicorn process can use.
+            limits:
+              cpu: "1"
+              memory: 512Mi
+          securityContext:
+            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
+            capabilities:
+              drop: [ALL]
+          volumeMounts:
+            - name: tmp
+              mountPath: /tmp
+      volumes:
+        - name: tmp
+          emptyDir: {}
+---
+# Headless: DNS answers with every ready pod, so nginx balances each request across them itself
+# instead of holding kept-alive connections to whichever pod one virtual IP picked.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: Service
+metadata:
+  name: api
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+spec:
+  clusterIP: None
+  selector:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+  ports:
+    - name: http
+      port: 8000
+      targetPort: http
+---
+# A drained node or a voluntary eviction never leaves fewer than two pods serving.
+apiVersion: policy/v1
+kind: PodDisruptionBudget
+metadata:
+  name: api
+spec:
+  minAvailable: 2
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: api

+# Postgres: one pod with its own volume, the same image compose runs. The password comes from the todo-db Secret.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: Service
+metadata:
+  name: db
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+spec:
+  # Headless: the name resolves straight to the pod, as a StatefulSet expects.
+  clusterIP: None
+  selector:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+  ports:
+    - name: postgres
+      port: 5432
+---
+apiVersion: apps/v1
+kind: StatefulSet
+metadata:
+  name: db
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+spec:
+  serviceName: db
+  replicas: 1
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+    spec:
+      automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      securityContext:
+        # 70 is the postgres user in the Alpine image.
+        runAsNonRoot: true
+        runAsUser: 70
+        runAsGroup: 70
+        fsGroup: 70
+        seccompProfile:
+          type: RuntimeDefault
+      containers:
+        - name: postgres
+          image: postgres:18.6-alpine3.24
+          env:
+            - name: POSTGRES_USER
+              value: todo
+            - name: POSTGRES_DB
+              value: todo
+            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: todo-db
+                  key: password
+          ports:
+            - name: postgres
+              containerPort: 5432
+          readinessProbe:
+            exec:
+              command: ["pg_isready", "-U", "todo", "-d", "todo"]
+            periodSeconds: 5
+          livenessProbe:
+            tcpSocket:
+              port: postgres
+            periodSeconds: 10
+            failureThreshold: 6
+          resources:
+            requests:
+              cpu: 250m
+              memory: 256Mi
+            limits:
+              cpu: "2"
+              memory: 1Gi

+            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
+            capabilities:
+              drop: [ALL]
+          volumeMounts:
+            # Postgres 18 images keep PGDATA at /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker, under this mount.
+            - name: data
+              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql
+            - name: run
+              mountPath: /var/run/postgresql

@@ -0,0 +1,195 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Deploy the app to a local k3d cluster: `python3 deploy/k3d/deploy.py up`, then open https://localhost:8443.
+
+`up` creates the cluster if it is missing, builds and imports the images for the current commit, creates the
+secrets if they are missing, then applies Postgres, the migration Job and the app, each after the one before is
+ready. `build`, `render` and `secrets` run one of those steps alone; `down` deletes the cluster and its data.
+Every command is printed before it runs. Secret values reach kubectl on stdin and are never printed or kept.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import logging
+import re
+import secrets
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+CLUSTER = "todo"
+NAMESPACE = "todo"
+CLUSTER_CONFIG = "deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml"
+PARTS = ("platform", "migrate", "app")
+# Each image and the folder it is built from, the same build compose runs.
+IMAGES = {"todo-api": "backend", "todo-web": "frontend"}
+SHORT_SHA = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{7,40}")
+# The names a browser or a test on the Mac uses for the cluster's front door.
+CERT_NAMES = ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1")
+TOOLS = ("docker", "k3d", "kubectl", "mkcert")
+URL = "https://localhost:8443"
+
+log = logging.getLogger("deploy")
+
+
+def release_files(sha: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Return the kustomization for each part of a release, keyed by its path under `deploy/.release/<sha>/`.
+
+    Each part builds on its k3d overlay and pins both images to the commit. The migration Job's name also
+    carries the commit, so each release runs it once and a repeat deploy of the same commit changes nothing.
+    """
+    if not SHORT_SHA.fullmatch(sha):
+        raise ValueError(f"not a short lowercase git sha: {sha!r}")
+    images = "".join(f"  - name: {name}\n    newTag: {sha}\n" for name in IMAGES)
+
+    def kustomization(part: str) -> str:
+        suffix = f"nameSuffix: -{sha}\n" if part == "migrate" else ""
+        return (
+            "apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1\nkind: Kustomization\n"
+            f"resources:\n  - ../../../overlays/k3d/{part}\n{suffix}images:\n{images}"
+        )
+
+    return {f"{part}/kustomization.yaml": kustomization(part) for part in PARTS}
+
+
+def rollout_steps(sha: str) -> list[list[str]]:
+    """Return the kubectl commands that roll out a written release, each waiting for the one before."""
+    release = f"deploy/.release/{sha}"
+    namespace = ["-n", NAMESPACE]
+    return [
+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/platform"],
+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "statefulset/db", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/migrate"],
+        ["kubectl", "wait", "--for=condition=complete", f"job/migrate-{sha}", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/app"],
+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/api", *namespace, "--timeout=300s"],
+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/web", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
+    ]
+
+
+def create_secret(name: str, data: dict[str, str], kind: str = "Opaque") -> tuple[list[str], str]:
+    """Return the command that creates a Secret and the manifest to send on its stdin, so no value is an argument."""
+    manifest = {
+        "apiVersion": "v1",
+        "kind": "Secret",
+        "metadata": {"name": name, "namespace": NAMESPACE},
+        "type": kind,
+        "stringData": data,
+    }
+    return ["kubectl", "create", "-f", "-"], json.dumps(manifest)
+
+
+def run(command: list[str], stdin: str | None = None) -> None:
+    """Print the command, run it from the repo root, and stop the deploy if it fails."""
+    log.info("+ %s", " ".join(command))
+    subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, input=stdin, text=True, check=True)
+
+
+def succeeds(command: list[str]) -> bool:
+    """Run a read-only check quietly and say whether it succeeded."""
+    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
+
+
+def current_sha() -> str:
+    """Return the short sha of the checked-out commit, the tag compose gives its images too."""
+    return subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
+    ).stdout.strip()
+
+
+def require_tools() -> None:
+    """Stop with the install command when a tool the deploy needs is missing."""
+    missing = [tool for tool in TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
+    if missing:
+        sys.exit(f"missing {', '.join(missing)}: brew install {' '.join(missing)} (see the README)")
+
+
+def ensure_cluster() -> None:
+    """Create the three-node cluster unless it already exists."""
+    if not succeeds(["k3d", "cluster", "get", CLUSTER]):
+        run(["k3d", "cluster", "create", "--config", CLUSTER_CONFIG])
+
+
+def build(sha: str) -> None:
+    """Build both images for the commit and copy them onto every node, so no pod pulls from a registry."""
+    tags = [f"{name}:{sha}" for name in IMAGES]
+    for tag, folder in zip(tags, IMAGES.values()):
+        run(["docker", "build", "-t", tag, folder])
+    run(["k3d", "image", "import", *tags, "--cluster", CLUSTER])
+
+
+def write_release(sha: str) -> Path:
+    """Write the release's kustomizations under `deploy/.release/<sha>/` and return that folder."""
+    folder = REPO / "deploy" / ".release" / sha
+    for path, text in release_files(sha).items():
+        (folder / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        (folder / path).write_text(text)
+    return folder
+
+
+def certificate() -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Make a certificate for the cluster's names, signed by mkcert's local authority, and return it as Secret data."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
+        cert, key = Path(folder) / "tls.crt", Path(folder) / "tls.key"
+        run(["mkcert", "-cert-file", str(cert), "-key-file", str(key), *CERT_NAMES])
+        return {"tls.crt": cert.read_text(), "tls.key": key.read_text()}
+
+
+def ensure_secrets() -> None:
+    """Create the namespace and each Secret that does not exist yet; existing ones, including your own, are kept."""
+    if not succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "namespace", NAMESPACE]):
+        # "--save-config" lets the later apply of the same namespace take it over without a warning.
+        run(["kubectl", "create", "namespace", NAMESPACE, "--save-config"])
+    # Hex keeps the password safe inside DATABASE_URL.
+    wanted = {
+        "todo-db": lambda: ({"password": secrets.token_hex(24)}, "Opaque"),
+        "todo-api": lambda: ({"jwt-secret": secrets.token_hex(32)}, "Opaque"),
+        "todo-tls": lambda: (certificate(), "kubernetes.io/tls"),
+    }
+    for name, make in wanted.items():
+        # "-o name" prints only the Secret's name, never its data.
+        if succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "secret", name, "-n", NAMESPACE, "-o", "name"]):
+            continue
+        data, kind = make()
+        command, payload = create_secret(name, data, kind)
+        run(command, stdin=payload)
+
+
+def up(sha: str) -> None:
+    """Run every step, from the cluster to a rolled-out app."""
+    require_tools()
+    ensure_cluster()
+    build(sha)
+    ensure_secrets()
+    write_release(sha)
+    for step in rollout_steps(sha):
+        run(step)
+    log.info("todo-app %s is running at %s", sha, URL)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Parse the subcommand and run it."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("up", "build", "render", "secrets", "down"))
+    parser.add_argument("--sha", help="the commit to deploy (default: the checked-out one)")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
+    sha = args.sha or current_sha()
+    actions = {
+        "up": lambda: up(sha),
+        "build": lambda: build(sha),
+        "render": lambda: log.info("wrote %s", write_release(sha)),
+        "secrets": ensure_secrets,
+        "down": lambda: run(["k3d", "cluster", "delete", CLUSTER]),
+    }
+    try:
+        actions[args.command]()
+    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
+        sys.exit(f"stopped: {' '.join(error.cmd)} exited with {error.returncode}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+"""Check the pure parts of deploy.py: the release it writes, the order of its steps, and how it passes secrets."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "deploy.py"
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("deploy", SCRIPT)
+assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+deploy = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+spec.loader.exec_module(deploy)
+
+SHA = "abc1234"
+
+
+class ReleaseTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_every_part_pins_both_images_to_the_commit(self) -> None:
+        for text in deploy.release_files(SHA).values():
+            self.assertIn("name: todo-api\n    newTag: abc1234", text)
+            self.assertIn("name: todo-web\n    newTag: abc1234", text)
+
+    def test_only_the_migration_job_name_carries_the_commit(self) -> None:
+        files = deploy.release_files(SHA)
+
+        self.assertIn("nameSuffix: -abc1234", files["migrate/kustomization.yaml"])
+        self.assertNotIn("nameSuffix", files["platform/kustomization.yaml"] + files["app/kustomization.yaml"])
+
+    def test_each_part_builds_on_its_k3d_overlay(self) -> None:
+        release = deploy.REPO / "deploy" / ".release" / SHA
+        for path, text in deploy.release_files(SHA).items():
+            [resource] = [line.strip()[2:] for line in text.splitlines() if line.startswith("  - ../")]
+            part = Path(path).parent.name
+            self.assertEqual((release / part / resource).resolve(), deploy.REPO / "deploy" / "overlays" / "k3d" / part)
+
+    def test_a_commit_that_is_not_a_short_hex_sha_is_refused(self) -> None:
+        for bad in ("", "main", "abc1234\nnameSuffix: x", "ABC1234"):
+            with self.subTest(bad=bad), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                deploy.release_files(bad)
+
+
+class StepsTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_the_app_rolls_out_only_after_the_migration_completes(self) -> None:
+        steps = [" ".join(step) for step in deploy.rollout_steps(SHA)]
+
+        def index(fragment: str) -> int:
+            return next(n for n, step in enumerate(steps) if fragment in step)
+
+        self.assertLess(index("rollout status statefulset/db"), index("apply -k deploy/.release/abc1234/migrate"))
+        self.assertLess(index("apply -k deploy/.release/abc1234/migrate"), index("wait --for=condition=complete"))
+        self.assertLess(index("wait --for=condition=complete"), index("apply -k deploy/.release/abc1234/app"))
+        self.assertEqual(index("job/migrate-abc1234"), index("wait --for=condition=complete"))
+
+
+class SecretTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_secret_values_go_on_stdin_never_in_the_command(self) -> None:
+        command, payload = deploy.create_secret("todo-db", {"password": "s3cret-value"})
+
+        self.assertNotIn("s3cret-value", " ".join(command))
+        self.assertEqual(command[-2:], ["-f", "-"])
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(payload)["stringData"], {"password": "s3cret-value"})
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(payload)["metadata"], {"name": "todo-db", "namespace": "todo"})
+
+    def test_a_tls_secret_has_the_tls_type(self) -> None:
+        _, payload = deploy.create_secret("todo-tls", {"tls.crt": "C", "tls.key": "K"}, kind="kubernetes.io/tls")
+
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(payload)["type"], "kubernetes.io/tls")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

577	+#!/usr/bin/env python3
578	+"""Deploy the app to a local k3d cluster: `python3 deploy/k3d/deploy.py up`, then open https://localhost:8443.
579	+
580	+`up` creates the cluster if it is missing, builds and imports the images for the current commit, creates the
581	+secrets if they are missing, then applies Postgres, the migration Job and the app, each after the one before is
582	+ready. `build`, `render` and `secrets` run one of those steps alone; `down` deletes the cluster and its data.
583	+Every command is printed before it runs. Secret values reach kubectl on stdin and are never printed or kept.
584	+"""
585	+from __future__ import annotations
586	+
587	+import argparse
588	+import json
589	+import logging
590	+import re
591	+import secrets
592	+import shutil
593	+import subprocess
594	+import sys
595	+import tempfile
596	+from pathlib import Path
597	+
598	+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
599	+CLUSTER = "todo"
600	+NAMESPACE = "todo"
601	+CLUSTER_CONFIG = "deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml"
602	+PARTS = ("platform", "migrate", "app")
603	+# Each image and the folder it is built from, the same build compose runs.
604	+IMAGES = {"todo-api": "backend", "todo-web": "frontend"}
605	+SHORT_SHA = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{7,40}")
606	+# The names a browser or a test on the Mac uses for the cluster's front door.
607	+CERT_NAMES = ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1")
608	+TOOLS = ("docker", "k3d", "kubectl", "mkcert")
609	+URL = "https://localhost:8443"
610	+
611	+log = logging.getLogger("deploy")
612	+
613	+
614	+def release_files(sha: str) -> dict[str, str]:
615	+    """Return the kustomization for each part of a release, keyed by its path under `deploy/.release/<sha>/`.
616	+
617	+    Each part builds on its k3d overlay and pins both images to the commit. The migration Job's name also
618	+    carries the commit, so each release runs it once and a repeat deploy of the same commit changes nothing.
619	+    """
620	+    if not SHORT_SHA.fullmatch(sha):
621	+        raise ValueError(f"not a short lowercase git sha: {sha!r}")
622	+    images = "".join(f"  - name: {name}\n    newTag: {sha}\n" for name in IMAGES)
623	+
624	+    def kustomization(part: str) -> str:
625	+        suffix = f"nameSuffix: -{sha}\n" if part == "migrate" else ""
626	+        return (
627	+            "apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1\nkind: Kustomization\n"
628	+            f"resources:\n  - ../../../overlays/k3d/{part}\n{suffix}images:\n{images}"
629	+        )
630	+
631	+    return {f"{part}/kustomization.yaml": kustomization(part) for part in PARTS}
632	+
633	+
634	+def rollout_steps(sha: str) -> list[list[str]]:
635	+    """Return the kubectl commands that roll out a written release, each waiting for the one before."""
636	+    release = f"deploy/.release/{sha}"
637	+    namespace = ["-n", NAMESPACE]
638	+    return [
639	+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/platform"],
640	+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "statefulset/db", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
641	+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/migrate"],
642	+        ["kubectl", "wait", "--for=condition=complete", f"job/migrate-{sha}", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
643	+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/app"],
644	+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/api", *namespace, "--timeout=300s"],
645	+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/web", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
646	+    ]
647	+
648	+
649	+def create_secret(name: str, data: dict[str, str], kind: str = "Opaque") -> tuple[list[str], str]:
650	+    """Return the command that creates a Secret and the manifest to send on its stdin, so no value is an argument."""
651	+    manifest = {
652	+        "apiVersion": "v1",
653	+        "kind": "Secret",
654	+        "metadata": {"name": name, "namespace": NAMESPACE},
655	+        "type": kind,
656	+        "stringData": data,
657	+    }
658	+    return ["kubectl", "create", "-f", "-"], json.dumps(manifest)
659	+
660	+
661	+def run(command: list[str], stdin: str | None = None) -> None:
662	+    """Print the command, run it from the repo root, and stop the deploy if it fails."""
663	+    log.info("+ %s", " ".join(command))
664	+    subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, input=stdin, text=True, check=True)
665	+
666	+
667	+def succeeds(command: list[str]) -> bool:
668	+    """Run a read-only check quietly and say whether it succeeded."""
669	+    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
670	+
671	+
672	+def current_sha() -> str:
673	+    """Return the short sha of the checked-out commit, the tag compose gives its images too."""
674	+    return subprocess.run(
675	+        ["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
676	+    ).stdout.strip()
677	+
678	+
679	+def require_tools() -> None:
680	+    """Stop with the install command when a tool the deploy needs is missing."""
681	+    missing = [tool for tool in TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
682	+    if missing:
683	+        sys.exit(f"missing {', '.join(missing)}: brew install {' '.join(missing)} (see the README)")
684	+
685	+
686	+def ensure_cluster() -> None:
687	+    """Create the three-node cluster unless it already exists."""
688	+    if not succeeds(["k3d", "cluster", "get", CLUSTER]):
689	+        run(["k3d", "cluster", "create", "--config", CLUSTER_CONFIG])
690	+
691	+
692	+def build(sha: str) -> None:
693	+    """Build both images for the commit and copy them onto every node, so no pod pulls from a registry."""
694	+    tags = [f"{name}:{sha}" for name in IMAGES]
695	+    for tag, folder in zip(tags, IMAGES.values()):
696	+        run(["docker", "build", "-t", tag, folder])
697	+    run(["k3d", "image", "import", *tags, "--cluster", CLUSTER])
698	+
699	+
700	+def write_release(sha: str) -> Path:
701	+    """Write the release's kustomizations under `deploy/.release/<sha>/` and return that folder."""
702	+    folder = REPO / "deploy" / ".release" / sha
703	+    for path, text in release_files(sha).items():
704	+        (folder / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
705	+        (folder / path).write_text(text)
706	+    return folder
707	+
708	+
709	+def certificate() -> dict[str, str]:
710	+    """Make a certificate for the cluster's names, signed by mkcert's local authority, and return it as Secret data."""
711	+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
712	+        cert, key = Path(folder) / "tls.crt", Path(folder) / "tls.key"
713	+        run(["mkcert", "-cert-file", str(cert), "-key-file", str(key), *CERT_NAMES])
714	+        return {"tls.crt": cert.read_text(), "tls.key": key.read_text()}
715	+
716	+
717	+def ensure_secrets() -> None:
718	+    """Create the namespace and each Secret that does not exist yet; existing ones, including your own, are kept."""
719	+    if not succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "namespace", NAMESPACE]):
720	+        # "--save-config" lets the later apply of the same namespace take it over without a warning.
721	+        run(["kubectl", "create", "namespace", NAMESPACE, "--save-config"])
722	+    # Hex keeps the password safe inside DATABASE_URL.
723	+    wanted = {
724	+        "todo-db": lambda: ({"password": secrets.token_hex(24)}, "Opaque"),
725	+        "todo-api": lambda: ({"jwt-secret": secrets.token_hex(32)}, "Opaque"),
726	+        "todo-tls": lambda: (certificate(), "kubernetes.io/tls"),
727	+    }
728	+    for name, make in wanted.items():
729	+        # "-o name" prints only the Secret's name, never its data.
730	+        if succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "secret", name, "-n", NAMESPACE, "-o", "name"]):
731	+            continue
732	+        data, kind = make()
733	+        command, payload = create_secret(name, data, kind)
734	+        run(command, stdin=payload)
735	+
736	+
737	+def up(sha: str) -> None:
738	+    """Run every step, from the cluster to a rolled-out app."""
739	+    require_tools()
740	+    ensure_cluster()
741	+    build(sha)
742	+    ensure_secrets()
743	+    write_release(sha)
744	+    for step in rollout_steps(sha):
745	+        run(step)
746	+    log.info("todo-app %s is running at %s", sha, URL)
747	+
748	+
749	+def main() -> None:
750	+    """Parse the subcommand and run it."""
751	+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
752	+    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("up", "build", "render", "secrets", "down"))
753	+    parser.add_argument("--sha", help="the commit to deploy (default: the checked-out one)")
754	+    args = parser.parse_args()
755	+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
756	+    sha = args.sha or current_sha()
757	+    actions = {
758	+        "up": lambda: up(sha),
759	+        "build": lambda: build(sha),
760	+        "render": lambda: log.info("wrote %s", write_release(sha)),
761	+        "secrets": ensure_secrets,
762	+        "down": lambda: run(["k3d", "cluster", "delete", CLUSTER]),
763	+    }
764	+    try:
765	+        actions[args.command]()
766	+    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
767	+        sys.exit(f"stopped: {' '.join(error.cmd)} exited with {error.returncode}")
768	+
769	+
770	+if __name__ == "__main__":
771	+    main()

Serving pinned Swagger UI files from the API, or disabling the page where cookies are secure, removes the third-party script before the app is public.

+# The API: three pods, one uvicorn process each, one per node. Any pod serves any request.
+apiVersion: apps/v1
+kind: Deployment
+metadata:
+  name: api
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+spec:
+  replicas: 3
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+  strategy:
+    # A new pod is ready before an old one leaves, so three keep serving through a release.
+    rollingUpdate:
+      maxSurge: 1
+      maxUnavailable: 0
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+    spec:
+      automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      # Covers the 20 s preStop sleep, uvicorn's 20 s drain and a margin.
+      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
+      topologySpreadConstraints:
+        - maxSkew: 1
+          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
+          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
+          labelSelector:
+            matchLabels:
+              app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+          # Counts only pods of the same release, so a rolling update can always place its new pod.
+          matchLabelKeys: [pod-template-hash]
+      securityContext:
+        runAsNonRoot: true
+        runAsUser: 10001
+        runAsGroup: 10001
+        seccompProfile:
+          type: RuntimeDefault
+      containers:
+        - name: api
+          image: todo-api
+          ports:
+            - name: http
+              containerPort: 8000
+          envFrom:
+            - configMapRef:
+                name: todo-config
+          env:
+            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: todo-db
+                  key: password
+            # Kubernetes fills in $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) from the variable above.
+            - name: DATABASE_URL
+              value: postgresql+asyncpg://todo:$(POSTGRES_PASSWORD)@db:5432/todo
+            - name: JWT_SECRET
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: todo-api
+                  key: jwt-secret
+          startupProbe:
+            httpGet:
+              path: /livez
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 2
+            failureThreshold: 30
+          livenessProbe:
+            httpGet:
+              path: /livez
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 10
+            failureThreshold: 3
+          readinessProbe:
+            httpGet:
+              path: /readyz
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 5
+            failureThreshold: 2
+          lifecycle:
+            # Kubernetes takes the pod out of the Service at once, but nginx re-reads DNS only every 10 s and
+            # the cluster DNS caches for 5 s. Serving 20 s more covers that, then SIGTERM starts uvicorn's drain.
+            # https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/#hook-handler-implementations
+            preStop:
+              sleep:
+                seconds: 20
+          resources:
+            requests:
+              cpu: 500m
+              memory: 256Mi
+            # One core is the most a single uvicorn process can use.
+            limits:
+              cpu: "1"
+              memory: 512Mi
+          securityContext:
+            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
+            capabilities:
+              drop: [ALL]
+          volumeMounts:
+            - name: tmp
+              mountPath: /tmp
+      volumes:
+        - name: tmp
+          emptyDir: {}
+---
+# Headless: DNS answers with every ready pod, so nginx balances each request across them itself
+# instead of holding kept-alive connections to whichever pod one virtual IP picked.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: Service
+metadata:
+  name: api
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+spec:
+  clusterIP: None
+  selector:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
+  ports:
+    - name: http
+      port: 8000
+      targetPort: http
+---
+# A drained node or a voluntary eviction never leaves fewer than two pods serving.
+apiVersion: policy/v1
+kind: PodDisruptionBudget
+metadata:
+  name: api
+spec:
+  minAvailable: 2
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: api

+# nginx: serves the SPA, sets the security headers and forwards /api/ to the API pods, as in compose.
+apiVersion: apps/v1
+kind: Deployment
+metadata:
+  name: web
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: web
+spec:
+  replicas: 2
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: web
+  strategy:
+    rollingUpdate:
+      maxSurge: 1
+      maxUnavailable: 0
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app.kubernetes.io/name: web
+    spec:
+      automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      topologySpreadConstraints:
+        - maxSkew: 1
+          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
+          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
+          labelSelector:
+            matchLabels:
+              app.kubernetes.io/name: web
+      securityContext:
+        # 101 is the nginx user in the unprivileged image.
+        runAsNonRoot: true
+        runAsUser: 101
+        runAsGroup: 101
+        seccompProfile:
+          type: RuntimeDefault
+      containers:
+        - name: web
+          image: todo-web
+          ports:
+            - name: http
+              containerPort: 8080
+          env:
+            # The full name, because nginx's resolver does not use the pod's DNS search list.
+            - name: API_HOST
+              value: api.todo.svc.cluster.local
+          readinessProbe:
+            httpGet:
+              path: /
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 5
+          livenessProbe:
+            tcpSocket:
+              port: http
+            periodSeconds: 10
+          lifecycle:
+            # Traefik follows the Service's endpoints directly, so a short pause covers it.
+            preStop:
+              sleep:
+                seconds: 5
+          resources:
+            requests:
+              cpu: 100m
+              memory: 32Mi
+            limits:
+              cpu: "1"
+              memory: 128Mi
+          securityContext:
+            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
+            capabilities:
+              drop: [ALL]
+          volumeMounts:
+            # The image's entrypoint writes the filled-in upstream config here at start.
+            - name: tmp
+              mountPath: /tmp
+      volumes:
+        - name: tmp
+          emptyDir: {}
+---
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: Service
+metadata:
+  name: web
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: web
+spec:
+  selector:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: web
+  ports:
+    - name: http
+      port: 8080
+      targetPort: http
+---
+apiVersion: policy/v1
+kind: PodDisruptionBudget
+metadata:
+  name: web
+spec:
+  minAvailable: 1
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: web

+# Runs the migrations once per release, with the API image; the deploy waits for it before rolling out the API.
+# It gets the database address alone, never the JWT secret.
+apiVersion: batch/v1
+kind: Job
+metadata:
+  name: migrate
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: migrate
+spec:
+  backoffLimit: 2
+  activeDeadlineSeconds: 300
+  # Kept a week for its logs. Running the same release again after that finds nothing left to migrate.
+  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 604800
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app.kubernetes.io/name: migrate
+    spec:
+      restartPolicy: Never
+      automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      securityContext:
+        runAsNonRoot: true
+        runAsUser: 10001
+        runAsGroup: 10001
+        seccompProfile:
+          type: RuntimeDefault
+      containers:
+        - name: migrate
+          image: todo-api
+          command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
+          env:
+            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: todo-db
+                  key: password
+            # Kubernetes fills in $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) from the variable above.
+            - name: DATABASE_URL
+              value: postgresql+asyncpg://todo:$(POSTGRES_PASSWORD)@db:5432/todo
+          resources:
+            requests:
+              cpu: 100m
+              memory: 128Mi
+            limits:
+              cpu: "1"
+              memory: 256Mi
+          securityContext:
+            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
+            capabilities:
+              drop: [ALL]
+          volumeMounts:
+            - name: tmp
+              mountPath: /tmp
+      volumes:
+        - name: tmp
+          emptyDir: {}

+# Postgres: one pod with its own volume, the same image compose runs. The password comes from the todo-db Secret.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: Service
+metadata:
+  name: db
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+spec:
+  # Headless: the name resolves straight to the pod, as a StatefulSet expects.
+  clusterIP: None
+  selector:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+  ports:
+    - name: postgres
+      port: 5432
+---
+apiVersion: apps/v1
+kind: StatefulSet
+metadata:
+  name: db
+  labels:
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+spec:
+  serviceName: db
+  replicas: 1
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app.kubernetes.io/name: db
+    spec:
+      automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      securityContext:
+        # 70 is the postgres user in the Alpine image.
+        runAsNonRoot: true
+        runAsUser: 70
+        runAsGroup: 70
+        fsGroup: 70
+        seccompProfile:
+          type: RuntimeDefault
+      containers:
+        - name: postgres
+          image: postgres:18.6-alpine3.24
+          env:
+            - name: POSTGRES_USER
+              value: todo
+            - name: POSTGRES_DB
+              value: todo
+            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: todo-db
+                  key: password
+          ports:
+            - name: postgres
+              containerPort: 5432
+          readinessProbe:
+            exec:
+              command: ["pg_isready", "-U", "todo", "-d", "todo"]
+            periodSeconds: 5
+          livenessProbe:
+            tcpSocket:
+              port: postgres
+            periodSeconds: 10
+            failureThreshold: 6
+          resources:
+            requests:
+              cpu: 250m
+              memory: 256Mi
+            limits:
+              cpu: "2"
+              memory: 1Gi
+          securityContext:
+            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
+            capabilities:
+              drop: [ALL]
+          volumeMounts:
+            # Postgres 18 images keep PGDATA at /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker, under this mount.
+            - name: data
+              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql
+            - name: run
+              mountPath: /var/run/postgresql
+            - name: tmp
+              mountPath: /tmp
+      volumes:
+        - name: run
+          emptyDir: {}
+        - name: tmp
+          emptyDir: {}
+  volumeClaimTemplates:
+    - metadata:
+        name: data
+      spec:
+        accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
+        resources:
+          requests:
+            storage: 1Gi

diff --git a/deploy/k3d/deploy.py b/deploy/k3d/deploy.py

+++ b/deploy/k3d/deploy.py
@@ -0,0 +1,195 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Deploy the app to a local k3d cluster: `python3 deploy/k3d/deploy.py up`, then open https://localhost:8443.
+
+`up` creates the cluster if it is missing, builds and imports the images for the current commit, creates the
+secrets if they are missing, then applies Postgres, the migration Job and the app, each after the one before is
+ready. `build`, `render` and `secrets` run one of those steps alone; `down` deletes the cluster and its data.
+Every command is printed before it runs. Secret values reach kubectl on stdin and are never printed or kept.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import logging
+import re
+import secrets
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+CLUSTER = "todo"
+NAMESPACE = "todo"
+CLUSTER_CONFIG = "deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml"
+PARTS = ("platform", "migrate", "app")
+# Each image and the folder it is built from, the same build compose runs.
+IMAGES = {"todo-api": "backend", "todo-web": "frontend"}
+SHORT_SHA = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{7,40}")
+# The names a browser or a test on the Mac uses for the cluster's front door.
+CERT_NAMES = ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1")
+TOOLS = ("docker", "k3d", "kubectl", "mkcert")
+URL = "https://localhost:8443"
+
+log = logging.getLogger("deploy")
+
+
+def release_files(sha: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Return the kustomization for each part of a release, keyed by its path under `deploy/.release/<sha>/`.
+
+    Each part builds on its k3d overlay and pins both images to the commit. The migration Job's name also
+    carries the commit, so each release runs it once and a repeat deploy of the same commit changes nothing.
+    """
+    if not SHORT_SHA.fullmatch(sha):
+        raise ValueError(f"not a short lowercase git sha: {sha!r}")
+    images = "".join(f"  - name: {name}\n    newTag: {sha}\n" for name in IMAGES)
+
+    def kustomization(part: str) -> str:
+        suffix = f"nameSuffix: -{sha}\n" if part == "migrate" else ""
+        return (
+            "apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1\nkind: Kustomization\n"
+            f"resources:\n  - ../../../overlays/k3d/{part}\n{suffix}images:\n{images}"
+        )
+
+    return {f"{part}/kustomization.yaml": kustomization(part) for part in PARTS}
+
+
+def rollout_steps(sha: str) -> list[list[str]]:
+    """Return the kubectl commands that roll out a written release, each waiting for the one before."""
+    release = f"deploy/.release/{sha}"
+    namespace = ["-n", NAMESPACE]
+    return [
+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/platform"],
+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "statefulset/db", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/migrate"],
+        ["kubectl", "wait", "--for=condition=complete", f"job/migrate-{sha}", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
+        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/app"],
+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/api", *namespace, "--timeout=300s"],
+        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/web", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
+    ]
+
+
+def create_secret(name: str, data: dict[str, str], kind: str = "Opaque") -> tuple[list[str], str]:
+    """Return the command that creates a Secret and the manifest to send on its stdin, so no value is an argument."""
+    manifest = {
+        "apiVersion": "v1",
+        "kind": "Secret",
+        "metadata": {"name": name, "namespace": NAMESPACE},
+        "type": kind,
+        "stringData": data,
+    }
+    return ["kubectl", "create", "-f", "-"], json.dumps(manifest)
+
+
+def run(command: list[str], stdin: str | None = None) -> None:
+    """Print the command, run it from the repo root, and stop the deploy if it fails."""
+    log.info("+ %s", " ".join(command))
+    subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, input=stdin, text=True, check=True)
+
+
+def succeeds(command: list[str]) -> bool:
+    """Run a read-only check quietly and say whether it succeeded."""
+    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
+
+
+def current_sha() -> str:
+    """Return the short sha of the checked-out commit, the tag compose gives its images too."""
+    return subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
+    ).stdout.strip()
+
+
+def require_tools() -> None:
+    """Stop with the install command when a tool the deploy needs is missing."""
+    missing = [tool for tool in TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
+    if missing:
+        sys.exit(f"missing {', '.join(missing)}: brew install {' '.join(missing)} (see the README)")
+
+
+def ensure_cluster() -> None:
+    """Create the three-node cluster unless it already exists."""
+    if not succeeds(["k3d", "cluster", "get", CLUSTER]):
+        run(["k3d", "cluster", "create", "--config", CLUSTER_CONFIG])
+
+
+def build(sha: str) -> None:
+    """Build both images for the commit and copy them onto every node, so no pod pulls from a registry."""
+    tags = [f"{name}:{sha}" for name in IMAGES]
+    for tag, folder in zip(tags, IMAGES.values()):
+        run(["docker", "build", "-t", tag, folder])
+    run(["k3d", "image", "import", *tags, "--cluster", CLUSTER])
+
+
+def write_release(sha: str) -> Path:
+    """Write the release's kustomizations under `deploy/.release/<sha>/` and return that folder."""
+    folder = REPO / "deploy" / ".release" / sha
+    for path, text in release_files(sha).items():
+        (folder / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        (folder / path).write_text(text)
+    return folder
+
+
+def certificate() -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Make a certificate for the cluster's names, signed by mkcert's local authority, and return it as Secret data."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
+        cert, key = Path(folder) / "tls.crt", Path(folder) / "tls.key"
+        run(["mkcert", "-cert-file", str(cert), "-key-file", str(key), *CERT_NAMES])
+        return {"tls.crt": cert.read_text(), "tls.key": key.read_text()}
+
+
+def ensure_secrets() -> None:
+    """Create the namespace and each Secret that does not exist yet; existing ones, including your own, are kept."""
+    if not succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "namespace", NAMESPACE]):
+        # "--save-config" lets the later apply of the same namespace take it over without a warning.
+        run(["kubectl", "create", "namespace", NAMESPACE, "--save-config"])
+    # Hex keeps the password safe inside DATABASE_URL.
+    wanted = {
+        "todo-db": lambda: ({"password": secrets.token_hex(24)}, "Opaque"),
+        "todo-api": lambda: ({"jwt-secret": secrets.token_hex(32)}, "Opaque"),
+        "todo-tls": lambda: (certificate(), "kubernetes.io/tls"),
+    }
+    for name, make in wanted.items():
+        # "-o name" prints only the Secret's name, never its data.
+        if succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "secret", name, "-n", NAMESPACE, "-o", "name"]):
+            continue
+        data, kind = make()
+        command, payload = create_secret(name, data, kind)
+        run(command, stdin=payload)

+def up(sha: str) -> None:
+    """Run every step, from the cluster to a rolled-out app."""
+    require_tools()
+    ensure_cluster()
+    build(sha)
+    ensure_secrets()
+    write_release(sha)
+    for step in rollout_steps(sha):
+        run(step)
+    log.info("todo-app %s is running at %s", sha, URL)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Parse the subcommand and run it."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("up", "build", "render", "secrets", "down"))
+    parser.add_argument("--sha", help="the commit to deploy (default: the checked-out one)")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
+    sha = args.sha or current_sha()
+    actions = {
+        "up": lambda: up(sha),
+        "build": lambda: build(sha),
+        "render": lambda: log.info("wrote %s", write_release(sha)),
+        "secrets": ensure_secrets,
+        "down": lambda: run(["k3d", "cluster", "delete", CLUSTER]),
+    }
+    try:
+        actions[args.command]()
+    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
+        sys.exit(f"stopped: {' '.join(error.cmd)} exited with {error.returncode}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Filled in by the image's entrypoint at start, so one image runs in compose and in Kubernetes:
+# https://github.com/nginx/docker-nginx/blob/master/entrypoint/20-envsubst-on-templates.sh
+# NGINX_LOCAL_RESOLVERS is the DNS server from /etc/resolv.conf: Docker's in compose, the cluster's in Kubernetes.
+# A short validity picks up replicas whose addresses change.
+resolver ${NGINX_LOCAL_RESOLVERS} valid=10s ipv6=off;
+
+upstream api {
+    # "resolve" re-reads the replicas' addresses from DNS; it needs a shared zone.
+    # https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#resolve
+    zone api 64k;
+    # API_HOST is the API's DNS name: "api" in compose, the headless Service's full name in Kubernetes.
+    server ${API_HOST}:8000 resolve;
+    # At most 16 idle connections per worker, 32 in all, well under each replica's 200-connection limit.
+    # https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#keepalive
+    keepalive 16;
+    # Shorter than uvicorn's 75 s, so nginx never reuses a connection the API is closing.
+    keepalive_timeout 60s;
+}
